title: Streaming chat: sideband provenance & metadata adapter for ergonomic events
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight sideband metadata adapter for Python streaming chat completions that attaches provenance and developer-friendly metadata to streaming events. Goal: let application code receive both canonical event payloads (tokens/choices) AND rich sideband signals (trace_id, model_variant, token_index_map, token_confidence_estimates, source_prompt_range) without breaking existing callback/iterator ergonomics. This adapter should be non-intrusive, low-latency, and opt-in by default.
acceptance_criteria:
- New adapter available at sdk.streaming.adapters.SidebandAdapter with opt-in config flag.
- Existing streaming iterator/callbacks remain backward compatible (no breaking API changes).
- Sideband metadata is emitted as a separate event type on the same stream ("sideband") and includes: trace_id, model_variant, event_seq, token_index_map (sparse), optional per-token confidence floats, and source_prompt_range.
- Unit and integration tests for interleaving main token events with sideband events.
- Example added to docs and quickstart showing how to consume sideband events and attach them to message records.
- Benchmarks show <5% p99 additional latency for typical small messages when adapter enabled.
design_decisions:
- Sideband events are separate event objects (not embedded in token deltas) to keep SDK stream parsers simple and to allow partial consumers to ignore sideband easily.
- Use short-lived UUID trace_id per request; correlate with runtime telemetry and console traces.
- token_index_map is encoded as list of (out_token_index, input_token_offset) pairs to avoid dense maps for long contexts.
- Confidence estimates are optional and can be omitted if model/runtime doesn't provide them.
- Adapter will expose two consumption modes: simple callback mode (on_sideband(event)) and iterator-aware transform (sideband_transform) that yields (main_event, sideband_dict) pairs.
- Default: adapter disabled to avoid changing existing telemetry; enable in request-level config or SDK client constructor.
api_examples:
# opt-in via client config:
from redwood import Client
client = Client(stream_sideband=True)
# streaming call
with client.chat_stream(model="redwood-x") as stream:
    for ev in stream:
        if ev.type == 'token':
            print(ev.text, end='')
        elif ev.type == 'sideband':
            # attach provenance to your local message object
            print('\nSIDEBAND:', ev.payload['trace_id'], ev.payload.get('token_confidence'))

# iterator-friendly transform:
from redwood.streaming.adapters import SidebandAdapter
adapter = SidebandAdapter()
for main, side in adapter.pairwise(stream):
    # main is the token/choice event, side is dict or None
    store_message_fragment(main.text, metadata=side or {})
telemetry_requirements:
- Emit trace.span.start and span.end with trace_id for each streaming request when sideband enabled.
- Add lightweight counters for sideband_emitted, sideband_missing_confidence, sideband_latency_ms.
- Ensure metrics are tagged by model_variant and deployment (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Logs should avoid including full token text; only include hashes or short IDs to satisfy privacy/legal for private deployments.
test_plan:
- Unit: adapter construction, pairwise pairing logic, edge cases (sideband before tokens, tokens without sideband).
- Integration: end-to-end streaming with instrumented runtime that returns sideband messages.
- Load: simulate 1000 concurrent small streams verify p99 latency < baseline * 1.05.
- Chaos: drop sideband messages in-flight and validate consumer resiliance; ensure no deadlocks or iterator hangs.
- Security: static scan of serializer; confirm no PII in sideband fields by default.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge feature behind flag; SDK unit tests green.
2) Internal dogfood by platform-sdks team using a sample app (chat-provenance-demo).
3) Gradual enablement in Console beta for selected customers for feedback.
4) Public docs and example release in py-sdk-2025.03.
5) Monitor telemetry for error rates for two weeks before GA.
